raw.assessment: The incumbent delivered every ordered design and achieved 25–31 minutes for unadjusted small covers. Its fitting check catches repairable defects, but seven seam reworks and a 37-minute median suggest preventable work without establishing its duration or cause. Rework concentrated in large covers (5/8 versus 2/14 medium); a common allowance is a plausible contributor, not a demonstrated cause. The concrete limiting observation is that both unsuccessful observed customer placements involved rounded corners missing from the reference tables: passing those tables cannot establish customer fit. Reported waste is below 8%, but its weight-based estimate does not establish area compliance.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may produce a size-dependent finished-fit error that a sew-before-bulk-cut checkpoint could detect and reduce.
openings.delta: Measure the transfer from cutting-card dimensions to finished dimensions before committing the remaining purchased stock.
openings.prediction: If allowance is responsible, comparable pieces should show a repeatable signed dimensional error by size; errors clustering instead by operator, direction or design would weaken that account.
openings.probe: Sew the first ordered cover of each size before bulk cutting. Record cut and sewn dimensions, operator, grain direction, design, fitting error and stage times. Measure retained offcuts along both axes through the stipulated wash test. Trial a revised allowance only if supported; verify remaining layouts by area against 8% waste before recutting.
assumptions: Checkpoint effort fits the three-week window and 350-unit budget.
Early covers provide diagnostic evidence, not proof of batch-wide performance.

openings.claim: Does corner geometry explain customer placement failures independently of tabletop length and width?
openings.delta: Test whether the reference-table check misses a geometry-specific installation requirement.
openings.prediction: A cover that passes the reference check but fails on a similarly dimensioned rounded table would distinguish geometry mismatch from nominal size mismatch.
openings.probe: Use the six willing customers to obtain actual dimensions and corner profiles, prioritizing nominal-only orders where possible. Compare first placement on reference and customer tables with similar dimensions and different corners; record where adjustment is needed. Use any supported pocket revision only after checking ordered appearance, removability and five-cycle wash survival.
assumptions: Participating customers include informative corner profiles and can demonstrate placement before dispatch.
Two observed failures do not establish corner shape as their cause.

raw.assessment: Large-cover rework and rounded-corner installation failures suggest different possible mismatches; their causes remain unestablished. Both combinations below are hypotheses requiring bounded trials.

openings.claim: Combine customer geometry confirmation with staged first-cover allowance calibration at the order-to-cutting-card interface.
openings.delta: Measurements alone cannot correct a faulty allowance; calibration on reference tables alone cannot detect customer corner geometry. Together they could calibrate construction against the intended installation before remaining panels are cut.
openings.prediction: The combination reduces first-placement failures more than either component alone, especially for large covers or tables differing from reference geometry.
openings.probe: Use six willing customers to record actual dimensions and corners. Compare four reversible offcut corner mockups: current practice, confirmed geometry only, calibrated allowance only, and both. Seat them against the measured target geometries; record mismatch and work time. Validate a first complete cover before releasing each affected cutting card, then record first-placement fit, design and total time for all 40.
assumptions: Customer measurements are sufficiently accurate and representative.
Trials and staged cutting fit the three-week window, existing machines, 350-unit budget and 8% area-waste ceiling.

openings.claim: Combine measured two-axis wash compensation with grain- and print-constrained nesting at the compensated-pattern-to-stock-layout interface.
openings.delta: Compensation could improve washed fit while consuming additional cloth; nesting could recover usable area without correcting shrinkage. Their interaction could accommodate necessary dimensional corrections within purchased stock.
openings.prediction: For stock exhibiting meaningful shrinkage, jointly planned compensated patterns retain washed fit while staying below 8% cutting waste by area; uncompensated layouts or compensation alone miss one of those outcomes.
openings.probe: Measure retained samples along both axes through the stipulated wash test. Compare compensated and current patterns under current and revised nesting, keeping visible design orientation fixed. Calculate area waste before cutting; verify a compensated sewn trial for fit, removability and wash survival.
assumptions: A feasible layout exists for required designs and sizes.
Measurement and nesting effort keep median total working time at or below 32 minutes.

openings.claim: Size-dependent allowance error and customer geometry mismatch are distinct hypotheses; combining calibration and geometry confirmation may improve both.
openings.discriminator: Repeatable signed error by size supports allowance; clustering by operator/grain/design weakens it. Reference success but customer failure at similar dimensions and different corners supports geometry. Both interventions outperforming either supports interaction.
openings.probe: Obtain six customers' dimensions/corners, prioritizing nominal-only orders. Compare current, geometry-only, calibration-only and combined offcut mockups. Sew first cover per size before bulk cutting; validate affected cards. Record cut/sewn dimensions, confounders, stage times and reference/customer placement. Check supported pocket revisions for appearance, removability and wash survival.
openings.uncertainty: Causes remain unestablished; two corner-associated failures and early covers are insufficient proof. Customer accuracy, representativeness and trial effort remain uncertain.

openings.claim: Two-axis wash compensation combined with grain/print-constrained nesting may preserve washed fit within purchased stock.
openings.discriminator: Compare current/compensated patterns crossed with current/revised nesting; joint success must preserve fit and area waste together.
openings.fit: Conditional preservation; retain ordered design orientation and sizes.
openings.probe: Measure retained samples along both axes through five wash cycles; calculate layout area waste before cutting/re-cutting. Verify compensated sewn fit, removability and wash survival.
openings.uncertainty: Sample representativeness, feasible layouts and added work time remain unknown; weight-estimated waste does not establish area compliance.

post_distill.decision: Run bounded probes using existing machines within 350 units and three weeks. Release layouts only within 8% area waste using purchased cloth. Measure all 40: at least 38 first-placement fits, every ordered design, median total work <=32 minutes. No success yet established.
